The separation matters because any definition of punishment should be value-neutral. A definition that already contains a justification would settle, by wording alone, whether imposing hardship for an offense is warranted, so retributive, deterrent, and reformative arguments could no longer be tested against the same practice. Keeping the concept descriptive leaves the aim of the institution open to judgment apart from the rules that decide who is punished and how much.

CONFIDENCE: 86
